claim: US business AI use was about 17–20%, while use among firms with four or fewer employees was below 20% and did not increase significantly from December 2025 to May 2026.

source.title: Large Firms With at Least 20 Employees Biggest AI Users
source.reliability_note: Nationally representative BTOS evidence, but broad AI use is not accounting-agent adoption and the question changed in late 2025.

notes: Counters immediate mass-market readiness; does not imply absence of a narrow early-adopter wedge.

claim: US AI adoption estimates differ materially by sampling, weighting, question framing, and unit of analysis; professional and financial services show relatively high uptake.

source.title: Monitoring AI Adoption in the US Economy
source.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
source.reliability_note: High-quality synthesis of three surveys, but partially shares BTOS ancestry with ACC-S01 and measures broad AI adoption.

notes: Shows both diffusion and denominator sensitivity; grouped with ACC-S01 to prevent double counting.

claim: Intuit announced an Accounting Agent for categorization, anomaly handling, and reconciliation inside QuickBooks with the customer kept in control.

source.title: Intuit Introduces Ground-Breaking Virtual Team of AI Agents to Fuel Growth for Businesses
source.reliability_note: Primary evidence of the issuer's product claim; financially interested and not independent evidence of retained adoption or efficacy.

notes: Supports capability and incumbent commitment while weakening a standalone entrant's distribution thesis.

claim: Intuit reported QuickBooks Online Accounting growth driven by price, customer growth, and mix, without a feature-specific retained-usage denominator for its accounting agents.

source.title: Intuit Reports Fourth Quarter and Full Year Fiscal 2026 Results
source.reliability_note: Auditable issuer filing context for company results, but it does not isolate accounting-agent adoption and remains interested-party evidence.

notes: Non-observation is weak counterevidence, not proof of poor retention; grouped with ACC-S03.

claim: Sage announced finance agents embedded in existing finance, HR, payroll, and operations systems, with people retaining control of final decisions.

source.title: Sage expands AI agents across finance, HR and operations
source.reliability_note: Primary evidence of Sage's product direction; financially interested and not neutral proof of production adoption.

notes: Confirms multi-incumbent commitment while increasing the platform-bundling threat.

claim: US tax professionals must maintain written information-security plans and oversee service providers that handle customer information.

source.title: Tips to help tax professionals protect client information
source.reliability_note: Authoritative guidance for US tax professionals; applicability varies for bookkeeping-only firms and specific product boundaries.

notes: Raises procurement, integration, and vendor-oversight cost for workflows touching taxpayer or customer information.

claim: GAO found inaccurate output, data-security and privacy risks, skills gaps, and authorization processes can slow AI deployment in a small-business-related government setting.

source.title: Artificial Intelligence: Uses and Risks for Small Business Contracting and Innovation Research
source.reliability_note: Independent government audit; transfer to private accounting firms is indirect and should be treated as a risk analogue, not a measured sector outcome.

notes: Useful counterexample to assuming capability announcements translate directly into authorized production use.
